raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`XPUAttentionImpl.forward` called `.contiguous()` on q, k and v before every
flash-attention call:

```python
q_ = query.contiguous().reshape(bsz * seqlen_q, nheads_q, d)
k_ = key.contiguous().reshape(bsz * seqlen_k, nheads_k, d)
v_ = value.contiguous().reshape(bsz * seqlen_k, nheads_k, d)
```

In FLUX.2's single-stream blocks q/k/v are head-packed, row-strided *slices* of
one fused projection output (`[tokens, 13824]` = `q | k | v | mlp`), so each
`.contiguous()` materialised a fresh `[tokens, heads, 128]` tensor — 3 copies
per block, 144 per DiT forward, 8.8 ms of profiled device time.

The sgl-kernel-xpu flash-attention kernel reads rows through their stride, so
the copies are not needed.

## Modifications

`multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/xpu_backend.py`: new
`_as_fa_input` helper used for q, k and v. It passes the tensor through
untouched when the `[rows, heads, head_dim]` view is one the kernel can read
directly — unit last-dim stride, heads packed at `head_dim`, row stride a
multiple of 8, 16-byte-aligned base — and otherwise copies exactly as before.

This is XPU-only; no other backend is touched.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel-level probe at the FLUX.2 shape (`[4608, 12, 128]`, token stride 13824):
output with strided q/k/v is `torch.equal` to output with contiguous inputs.
The same probe also confirms the kernel accepts a strided *output* buffer and
leaves neighbouring columns untouched (not used by this PR — see follow-up).

`test_flux2_xpu_norm_fusions.py::test_attention_reads_fused_projection_slices_in_place`
(added here): asserts `_as_fa_input` returns the input's own `data_ptr` for a
fused-projection slice, and that `XPUAttentionImpl.forward` gives a
`torch.equal` result for strided and contiguous inputs. The file is now 6 cases,
all passing on Arc Pro B70.

End to end: no bit-exact fallback warnings; images differ from the parent commit
only at oneCCL run-to-run noise level (see PR 2).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End to end (FLUX.2-dev, 1024x1024, 8 steps, bf16, eager, warm, TP4 on 4x
Arc Pro B70), 2 runs per side:

| | denoise (8 steps) | per DiT forward |
|---|---|---|
| parent commit | 6.140 / 6.129 s | — |
| this commit | 6.077 / 6.095 s | **−6 ms (−0.8%)** |

torch.profiler: the 144 `aten::copy_` kernels per forward (8.8 ms) are gone.
Flash attention itself costs ~1.2 ms more per forward with strided reads, so the
net saving is smaller than the copies removed.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -65,6 +65,27 @@ def _get_cu_seqlens(device_index: int, bsz: int, seqlen: int) -> torch.Tensor:
     )
 
 
+def _as_fa_input(t: torch.Tensor, rows: int, heads: int, head_dim: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``t`` as the ``[rows, heads, head_dim]`` flash-attention input, copying only if needed.
+
+    The kernel reads rows through their stride, so a head-packed row-strided view
+    (e.g. q/k/v slices of a fused projection output) is used in place; measured
+    bit-identical to the contiguous input.
+    """
+    try:
+        view = t.view(rows, heads, head_dim)
+    except RuntimeError:
+        return t.contiguous().view(rows, heads, head_dim)
+    if (
+        view.stride(-1) == 1
+        and view.stride(-2) == head_dim
+        and view.stride(0) % 8 == 0
+        and view.data_ptr() % 16 == 0
+    ):
+        return view
+    return view.contiguous()
+
+
 class XPUAttentionImpl(AttentionImpl):
     def __init__(
         self,

         self.assertEqual(returned.data_ptr(), gemm_input[..., 1536:].data_ptr())
         self.assertTrue(torch.equal(gemm_input, expected))
 
+    def test_attention_reads_fused_projection_slices_in_place(self):
+        # Single-block q/k/v are row-strided slices of the fused projection
+        # output; the XPU backend must feed them to flash attention without a
+        # copy and get the same result as contiguous inputs.
+        from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends import (
+            xpu_backend,
+        )
+
+        torch.manual_seed(5)
+        tokens, heads, head_dim = 256, 12, 128
+        proj = torch.randn(1, tokens, 13824, device="xpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        q, k, v = (
+            proj[..., i * heads * head_dim : (i + 1) * heads * head_dim].view(
+                1, tokens, heads, head_dim
+            )
+            for i in range(3)
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            xpu_backend._as_fa_input(q, tokens, heads, head_dim).data_ptr(),
+            q.data_ptr(),
+        )
+        impl = xpu_backend.XPUAttentionImpl(
+            num_heads=heads,
+            head_size=head_dim,
+            causal=False,
+            softmax_scale=head_dim**-0.5,
+        )
+        expected = impl.forward(q.contiguous(), k.contiguous(), v.contiguous())
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(impl.forward(q, k, v), expected))
+
     def test_launchers_reject_layouts_they_do_not_replicate(self):
